clue.text: Disaffected Tory 10 getting stuck into the whisky

definitions.note: the clue word is an adjective; the answer is a noun for a disaffected person

indicators.note: something stuck into another thing ends up lodged inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: malt is a kind of whisky
Con is the abbreviation for Conservative, the Tory party
the number written as a word

explanation.surface: A rebellious Conservative MP drowns their sorrows in Scotch.
explanation.walkthrough: The 10 looks like a cross-reference to another clue, as numbers in Telegraph clues usually are, but here it is simply the number written out.
explanation.definitionFit: A malcontent is a dissatisfied, rebellious person, the noun counterpart of someone feeling disaffected.

clue.text: Human bomb finally changing sides

indicators.note: the last letter swaps one side for the other, right becoming left

parts.note: a mortar bomb is a shell fired from a mortar
R for right is replaced by L for left

explanation.surface: A human bomber defects to the other side at the last moment.
explanation.walkthrough: The final R of MORTAR (right) changes side to L (left).
explanation.definitionFit: Mortal as an adjective describes beings subject to death, which is what being human entails.

clue.text: What Macron chews? European veg

definitions.meaning: first meaning: légume is French for vegetable, food for the French president
second meaning: a pod vegetable such as a pea or bean, the word itself borrowed from European French

explanation.walkthrough: Emmanuel Macron is the French president, so what he eats is a French vegetable, a légume; in English the same word names peas and beans.
explanation.definitionFit: In French légume means any vegetable, while English uses legume for pod-bearing plants like beans, peas and lentils.

clue.text: It challenges its students; previous ninety failed

indicators.note: something that has failed has broken down, so these letters fall apart and are rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A demanding college laments that ninety previous candidates did not pass.
explanation.walkthrough: The Open University is the UK's distance-learning university, open to adults without prior qualifications.
explanation.definitionFit: Any university sets demanding coursework and examinations for those enrolled, so this institution is described by what it does to learners.

clue.text: This PM says cracknel, cut regularly, is a teatime treat

indicators.note: cutting at a regular interval removes every other letter and keeps the rest

parts.note: first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters of these words
first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister declares a crunchy sweet, sliced up, perfect for afternoon tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This PM says' looks like a political quotation, but it is just raw letters; the cut applies to both phrases. Cracknel is a crisp brittle biscuit or toffee.
explanation.definitionFit: Tipsy cake is a British dessert of sponge soaked in sherry or wine, served as a sweet treat at tea.

clue.text: Noise coming from The Nag's Head?

definitions.text: Noise coming from The Nag's Head?

parts.note: surface reading: a common British pub name, so the noise of a busy bar
setter's reading: the sound that comes from an old horse's mouth

explanation.walkthrough: The Nag's Head is a familiar British pub name, suggesting pub chatter; read literally, a nag is a horse and its head makes the noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse's characteristic call is a high whinnying sound, and a nag is an old or tired horse.

clue.text: Starts to sell warrants at Paris exchange

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters, which are the ones kept

parts.note: opening letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: A trader begins offloading warrants on the Paris bourse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paris exchange' reads as the stock market, but exchange stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To swap is to trade one thing for another, a common synonym for the verb or noun meaning trade.

clue.text: African capital with independent hospital fine for nursing English

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, so one piece cradles another inside it

parts.note: W is the standard abbreviation for with
Ind is the abbreviation for independent
H as on road signs
OK means fine, all right
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A capital city in Africa boasts a private hospital good at caring for English patients.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests healthcare; nursing is the containment, OK holding E.
explanation.definitionFit: Windhoek is the capital city of Namibia, in south-western Africa.

clue.text: Quiet student Mike punches lad in Devon port

indicators.note: a punch drives in, so one piece is forced inside another

parts.note: p for piano, the musical instruction to play quietly
L for learner, as on a learner driver's plate
a lad is a young man
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A quiet student called Mike hits a boy in a Devon harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: Mike looks like the student's name, but it is a letter from the radio alphabet, slipped in after the first letter of YOUTH.
explanation.definitionFit: Plymouth is a major naval and ferry port on the south coast of Devon, a county in south-west England.

clue.text: Patented SSRI — an amazing drug

indicators.note: something amazing leaves one bewildered, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An advert praises a branded SSRI as a wonder drug.
explanation.walkthrough: An SSRI (selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor) is itself an example of the answer, so the surface tells the truth while its letters are scrambled.
explanation.definitionFit: Medication taken to treat depression is a type of pharmaceutical, so the answer is one kind of medicine.

clue.text: Rascal, libertine having good heart

indicators.note: to have something is to hold it, so one piece holds another
a heart lies at the centre, so the inserted piece goes into the middle

parts.note: a roué is a debauched man, a libertine
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A scoundrel and womaniser who is nonetheless kind at heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heart' says where G goes: into the middle of ROUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue is a dishonest but often likeable scoundrel, a close synonym for a mischievous rascal.

clue.text: Pathetic state every now and again opposing Ms Pelosi

indicators.note: something done every now and again happens intermittently, so only some letters are kept, at intervals

parts.note: second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters
Nancy Pelosi, former Speaker of the US House of Representatives

explanation.surface: A sad country keeps clashing with the American politician Nancy Pelosi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pathetic' here is in its older sense of arousing pity, not contemptible.
explanation.definitionFit: Poignancy is the quality of evoking pity or sadness, which is what pathos, the root of pathetic, means.

clue.text: Arsenal warm our yogurt pots

indicators.note: pots are containers, so these words hold the answer inside them

parts.note: runs across the three words

explanation.surface: A football club's kitchen heats up tubs of yogurt.
explanation.walkthrough: Arsenal suggests the London football club; here it is the store of weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: An armoury is a place where weapons and ammunition are stored, exactly what an arsenal is.

clue.text: Routine tool for raking dry grass, it's said

definitions.note: the clue word is an adjective; the answer is an exclamation of weary resignation

indicators.note: something said is spoken out loud, so its sound matters, not its spelling

parts.note: hay is dry grass and a hoe is a garden tool, together a tool for hay

explanation.surface: A farm implement is described for gathering hay.
explanation.walkthrough: Heigh-ho is the sigh of someone facing the same dull round again, as in the Seven Dwarfs' work song.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation expresses boredom or resignation at tedious, everyday tasks, so it sums up a mundane routine.

clue.text: Quarrel — senior detective sergeant angrily arrests me

indicators.note: to arrest is to take into custody, so one piece is held inside another
acting angrily is acting in a wild temper, so these letters are thrown about

parts.note: a Detective Inspector outranks a sergeant
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A row breaks out as a furious senior officer and sergeant take the speaker into custody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Senior detective' is DI, a Detective Inspector, the rank above sergeant; the scrambled letters then take in ME.
explanation.definitionFit: A disagreement is an argument or difference of opinion, so it serves as a plain synonym for a row.

clue.text: President who could become vote loser

indicators.note: what could become something else is changed in form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A head of state who might end up being defeated at the ballot box.
explanation.walkthrough: Ironically both Roosevelts were notable election winners; Franklin won four times.
explanation.definitionFit: Theodore and Franklin D. Roosevelt were both Presidents of the United States.

clue.text: Collect some brass emblems

indicators.note: some means only part, so a portion of the following words is taken

parts.note: spans the end of one word and most of the next

explanation.surface: Gathering up a few metal badges.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits across the two words, missing only the outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To assemble is to gather things or people together, a direct synonym of the verb collect.

clue.text: Record one record on the radio, broadcast late at night

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
Roman numeral one

indicators.note: what is on the radio is heard, not seen, so sound replaces spelling

parts.note: a log is a written record; this ending is said the same way

explanation.surface: A disc jockey plays a track on air during the late shift.
explanation.walkthrough: The Epilogue was a short religious programme that closed British TV and radio schedules late at night.
explanation.definitionFit: The station's final programme of the day was a brief reflective item named after the closing speech of a play.

clue.text: Top jurists: Diana Ross reportedly apprehended?

parts.note: Diana Ross was lead singer of the Motown group the Supremes

indicators.note: a report is something spoken, so a word is replaced by one that sounds the same

parts.note: apprehended means arrested; in non-rhotic speech the two words match

explanation.surface: Senior judges hear that the soul singer has been arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: A Supreme caught is Diana Ross apprehended; in British speech, which drops the R, caught and court sound identical.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest court in a country is staffed by its most senior judges, so the bench stands for the jurists themselves.

clue.text: Gloss over title defended by the Spanish

indicators.note: what is defended is protected on all sides, so one piece is surrounded by another

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
a title is the name of a work

explanation.surface: Someone tries to hide a disputed title that Spain is fighting to keep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gloss over' suggests hiding a problem, but here it means literally coating a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To enamel something is to coat it with a hard glossy finish, so the verb means put a shiny layer onto.

clue.text: Heavy, loaded, filled with energy

indicators.note: something filled has content placed inside it, so one piece holds another

parts.note: laden means loaded, carrying a burden
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A list of words for being weighed down, with a twist of vigour at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as three near-synonyms, but energy is what fills the second word.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaden literally means made of lead and figuratively means weighty or sluggish, a synonym for ponderous and dull.

clue.text: Recruits nurses to maintain register

indicators.note: to maintain is to hold up and keep, so one piece holds another within it

parts.note: ENs are Enrolled Nurses
a register is a list of names

explanation.surface: New hospital staff are assigned to keep the patient register up to date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recruits' looks like a noun for new staff, but it is a verb; EN, an Enrolled Nurse, is a standard crossword nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlist someone is to sign them up for the armed forces or a cause, which is what an organisation does when it takes people on.

clue.text: Challenge for you: very large, very easy at first

definitions.note: the clue phrase is a noun phrase; the answer is the verb a solver is challenged to do

parts.note: so means very, as in so good
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
v is the abbreviation for very

indicators.note: what comes at first is the beginning, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: opening letter only

explanation.surface: A puzzle setter promises a huge challenge that starts off simple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very' appears twice and gives different letters each time, first SO and then V.
explanation.definitionFit: The challenge set for the crossword reader is to work out the answer, which is exactly the act of finding solutions.

clue.text: Core of German city Cologne evacuated

parts.note: Essen is a city in the Ruhr region of Germany

indicators.note: an evacuated building is emptied of its contents, so only the outer shell remains

parts.note: first and last letters only

explanation.surface: The centre of a German city is cleared of people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Core of German city' reads as one phrase, but Core alone is the definition and Cologne is a second city.
explanation.definitionFit: The essence of something is its fundamental nature, the heart or centre that makes it what it is.

clue.text: Table leg knocked over a trifle

indicators.note: something knocked over is upset and in disarray, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone bumps a table and sends a pudding flying.
explanation.walkthrough: Trifle looks like the British layered dessert, but it means something of little importance; bagatelle is also a table game, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A bagatelle is a thing of little value or importance, the same as a trifle in its noun sense.

clue.text: Carrying a gun, husband left injured

indicators.note: whatever has left has gone away, so a letter departs

parts.note: harmed means hurt
h is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A gunman's spouse has been left wounded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like a direction or verb about abandonment, but it removes H from HARMED.
explanation.definitionFit: To be armed is to bear a weapon, so someone toting a firearm fits the adjective.

clue.text: Still time to break off affair

indicators.note: breaking off a piece removes it, so a letter is snapped away

parts.note: an affair is an occasion or event
t is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: There is yet an opportunity to end a romantic liaison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Affair' suggests romance, but here it means an occasion; Still is the adverb, as in even better or still better.
explanation.definitionFit: Even and still both intensify a comparison, as in still more or even more, so they are interchangeable adverbs.

clue.text: Running tenth lap, Olympian exhausted in the event

indicators.note: running freely means moving about, so these letters change places

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: something exhausted is drained of its contents, leaving only the outer letters

parts.note: first and last letters only

explanation.surface: An Olympic athlete is worn out on the tenth lap of their race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Running' and 'exhausted' read as athletic description, but one scrambles letters and the other empties a word.
explanation.definitionFit: The pentathlon is a five-discipline athletic competition, one of the contests held at the Olympic Games.
